chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from 'Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Do not pray behind the exaggerator (in price or status), even if he recites with your recitation, and the unknown (one whose status is unclear), and the one who openly commits sin, even if he is moderate (in other matters).

key_terms.الْغَالِي: The exaggerator (often referring to Ghulat who attribute divinity to Imams)
key_terms.الْمَجْهُولِ: The unknown (one whose reliability or status is not well-known)
key_terms.الْمُجَاهِرِ بِالْفِسْقِ: The one who openly commits sin
key_terms.مُقْتَصِدًا: Moderate (in other virtues despite the specific flaw)

ai.seo_question: Who are the specific types of Imams excluded from leading congregational prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that the validity of congregational prayer depends not only on the Imam's ritual correctness but also on his theological and moral integrity. It specifically excludes the *Ghali* (extremists who attribute divinity to the Imams), the *Majhul* (whose identity is unverified), and the *Mujahir bil-Fisq* (open sinner), ensuring the congregation's unity in both belief and practice. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *Adalah* (justice/uprightness) as a prerequisite for leadership in worship.
